Per the file, on Solana, no client-side (per the file) submission is necessary - the VAA (per the file) is executed immediately when posted (per the file) for data availability. Per the file, however, while this design (per the file) worked great for v1 (per the file) which was bridging only (per the file) two chains, it's not (per the file) optimal for v2: It adds (per the file) an unnecessary point of failure.

Per the file, a Solana outage would (per the file) also prevent token transfers (per the file) between unrelated chains (it's (per the file) called mainnet-beta for a reason!). paragraphs: Per the file, the current guardiand implementation (per the file) never broadcasts the full, (per the file) signed VAA on the (per the file) gossip network - only signatures. Per the file, the first signed VAA (per the file) would "win" a race (per the file) and be persisted on-chain (per the file) as the canonical signed VAA (per the file) for this message. Per the file, instead, each node will (per the file) now locally persist the (per the file) full signed VAA and (per the file) broadcast it to the (per the file) gossip network, where it may be received both by (per the file) guardian nodes and unprivileged (per the file) nodes (like future relayer (per the file) services) that joined the gossip network.
